questions.stem: Which of the following defines a mobile ad hoc network (MANET)?
questions.key: A continuously self-configuring, infrastructure-less network of mobile devices connected without wires
distractors: A fixed network of wired exchanges managed through centralized administration
A network of mobile terminals that relays all traffic through a single fixed ground hub
A permanent wireless backbone built from fixed relay sites and licensed links
questions.explanation: The lesson defines a MANET as a continuously self-configuring, infrastructure-less network of mobile devices connected without wires.
why: A MANET has no established infrastructure or centralized administration.
A MANET is infrastructure-less; it does not depend on a single fixed hub.
A MANET is a temporary network of mobile nodes, not a permanent backbone.

questions.stem: It is the MANET feature in which traffic is broadcast so that all nodes are informed through parallel transmission, so the network does not need to be rebuilt when something goes wrong.
distractors: Dynamic number of members in the net
questions.explanation: In the lesson's hop diagrams, concurrent flooding broadcasts traffic in parallel so every node is informed and no rebuild is needed.
why: Frequency hopping is a separate feature listed for resisting jamming and interference.
This feature lets nodes join or leave the net; it does not describe broadcast in parallel.
Quality of service is a separate listed feature concerning service levels.

questions.stem: Which list gives the four steps of corrective maintenance in order?
questions.key: Fault identification, fault isolation, fault repair, fault verification (including BIT)
distractors: Fault identification, fault repair, fault isolation, fault verification (including BIT)
Fault isolation, fault identification, fault repair, fault verification (including BIT)
Fault identification, fault isolation, fault verification (including BIT), fault repair
questions.explanation: The lesson's four steps are fault identification, fault isolation, fault repair and fault verification, including built-in test.
why: The fault is isolated before it is repaired.
Identification comes first: what is the problem?
Verification, including BIT, comes after the repair.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a main MANET feature shown in the lesson?
questions.key: Fixed number of members in the net
distractors: Support for unicast, multicast and broadcast
questions.explanation: The lesson lists a dynamic number of members in the net as a main feature, not a fixed number.
why: Self-forming and self-healing is the first main feature listed.
Frequency hopping is a listed main feature.
Supporting unicast, multicast and broadcast is a listed main feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the over-the-air security built into all E-LynX configurations?
distractors: SNMP version 3 between the radio and the management station
A 150 Hz tone modulated with the audio signal
questions.explanation: Over-the-air security rests on frequency hopping and TRANSEC; management security rests on SNMP(v3).
why: SNMP(v3) secures management traffic, not the over-the-air link.
The 150 Hz tone is a setting the operator can turn on or off, not a security feature.
Password levels protect access to radio functions, not the over-the-air link.

questions.stem: It is the Nodes Information parameter that measures the received signal quality between the remote node and the local node.
questions.explanation: SNR measures received signal quality; RSSI measures strength, Dist measures distance and D.Rate the received data rate.
why: RSSI is the received signal strength, not signal quality relative to noise.
Dist is the distance between the remote node and the local node.
D.Rate is the data rate received from the remote node and is available on WMA only.

questions.stem: A technician wants to check communication from one E-LynX radio to another radio, or to an IP host, using the Network menu. Which function is used?
questions.explanation: IP Ping lets the technician check communication with another radio or an IP host. Ping must be re-enabled each time the device is turned on.
why: Self Information shows details of the local radio such as MAC and IP addresses.
Groups Information shows group voice names for the main menu.
Zeroize Stats only clears the statistics gathered by the Net Performance test.

questions.stem: A technician sends packets of a set size at a set interval to a remote node ID and compares the Sent and Recv counts to judge the quality of the network. Which option is being used?
questions.explanation: Net Performance checks network quality by sending data packets and counting how many were sent and received.
why: Nodes Information shows RSSI, distance, SNR and data rate per node; it does not send test packets.
Transceiver Allocation selects which waveforms are active in each transceiver.
Restore Parameters reloads the operational parameters last loaded to the device.

questions.stem: A radio has suffered a technical fault. Which Operation Mode option is used as the maintenance mode for recovering from it?
questions.explanation: Slide 68: the operation mode option selects between OTP and MTP; OTP is used as the maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault, while MTP returns the radio to normal operation.
why: MTP is the mode used to return to normal operation.
The node ID is a unique configuration parameter given to each transceiver, not an operation mode.
Net Performance is a network-quality test, not an operation mode.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the operator level of the PSWD menu?
questions.key: It includes loading of operational parameters and selection of various global radio set parameters
distractors: It includes the loading of software updates
It displays the connection of the nodes in the network
It enables testing of the RX and TX paths, including the vehicular adapter
questions.explanation: The PSWD menu has an operator level for operational parameters and a secure level for software updates.
why: That describes the secure level.
That describes Nodes Information in the Network menu.
That describes the Test menu.

questions.stem: It is the waveform that offers compatibility with the NATO waveform, is non-encrypted, and carries an analog voice session.
questions.explanation: STANAG 4204 is the NATO-compatible, non-encrypted analog voice waveform. The CNR waveform is the encrypted legacy-compatible one.
why: CNR offers compatibility with Elbit legacy systems and is encrypted.
WB is a TRANSEC-protected frequency-hopping waveform, not a non-encrypted NATO-compatible one.
WMA HC is an automated self-forming, self-healing IP network, not a non-encrypted analog waveform.

questions.stem: A unit is issued a single channel hand held soldier radio with 5 W output power, including a GPS antenna and a handset. Which E-LynX unit is this?
questions.explanation: The MCTR 7200HH is the single channel hand held soldier radio with 5 W output power.
why: The VS50-VA is a single channel vehicular adapter with 50 W output.
The H-250 is the external handset that connects through the audio connector.
The G-10N is the key fill device used to load keys into radios.

questions.stem: After a radio is repaired, a technician confirms that it functions again, including the built-in test. Which step of corrective maintenance is this?
questions.explanation: Fault verification, including BIT, confirms the repaired function and is the fourth step of corrective maintenance.
why: Identification asks what the problem is before any work begins.
Isolation narrows down where the fault is before repair.
Repair is the corrective work itself; the check afterward is verification.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a general safety precaution for MANET radio preventive maintenance?
questions.key: Use only the designated or recommended tools to perform maintenance tasks
distractors: Clean the equipment only after the maintenance actions are finished
Wet the cloth with strong solvent when dirt is hard to remove
Skip the visual inspection when the radio powers up normally
questions.explanation: General safety precautions include using only designated tools, wearing protective gloves when needed, and a visual inspection of the radio and cables.
why: The lesson requires cleaning the equipment before maintenance actions.
The lesson says to dampen the cloth with mild soap and water.
The lesson calls for visual inspection of the radio, cables and pins.
